articles.title: Zambia’s copper boom attracts billions in investment, but who benefits?
articles.excerpt: Lusaka, Zambia – Zambia is attracting billions of dollars in mining investment as it seeks to become a significant supplier of minerals critical to the global energy transition. But as foreign compani...
articles.body_text:
Lusaka, Zambia – Zambia is attracting billions of dollars in mining investment as it seeks to become a significant supplier of minerals critical to the global energy transition. But as foreign companies expand operations and new projects come on stream, questions are mounting over whether common Zambians are benefitting from the country’s growing mineral wealth.

President Hakainde Hichilema said more than $12bn had been invested in Zambia’s mining sector since 2022, as the government pushes to increase copper production and attract new investors.

Leading investors include Canadian companies First Quantum Minerals and Barrick Mining Corporation, India’s Vedanta Resources and China Nonferrous Metal Mining Group (CNMC).

Abu Dhabi-based International Resources Holding (IRH) has also emerged as a leading investor after committing $1.1bn to recapitalise Mopani Copper Mines, previously owned by Glencore. The investment gave IRH a 51 percent stake in the mine, with state-owned ZCCM Investments Holdings retaining 49 percent.

Alongside large-scale mining projects, the Copperbelt province has also seen the expansion of smaller Chinese-owned mineral-processing plants, some sourcing ore from artisanal and small-scale miners. Their growth has raised concerns about safety standards, regulatory oversight and environmental protection.

The government has sought to restore investor confidence through tax incentives and a more predictable fiscal framework, following years of frequent changes to mining tax policies under the former Patriotic Front government, which ruled Zambia between 2011 and 2021.

To accelerate mineral exploration, Zambia is undertaking a nationwide high-resolution aerial geophysical survey aimed at improving geological information and identifying previously unexplored mineral deposits. The survey is now about 98 percent complete, according to the Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development.

The government has set an ambitious target of increasing annual copper production to 3 million tonnes by 2031, from less than 1 million tonnes in recent years.

“We can do with our copper, cobalt, nickel, lithium, manganese and rare earth metals, which we now know we have in this country for our people, what the UAE has done with oil and gas for its people and their economy,” Hichilema told delegates at the Zambia Mining and Investment Forum in Lusaka on October 19.

Beyond increasing production, Zambia is also seeking to expand value addition to copper, a key material in electric vehicles and renewable energy infrastructure.

Historically, the country has exported copper cathodes to China and other industrialised countries. But the government wants Zambia to play a more active role in the global transition to a low-carbon economy by developing domestic mineral processing and manufacturing capacity.

Africa’s two leading copper producers, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Zambia, are also exploring a partnership with South Africa to develop an electric vehicle battery manufacturing industry.

“DRC and ourselves are doing something on EV materials so we can build a joint venture with South Africa, which is ahead of us in the motor industry, so that the motor vehicles produced out of South African production lines have Congolese and Zambian inputs of the EV battery,” Hichilema said.

The proposed partnership reflects growing efforts by African mineral producers to move beyond exporting raw materials and capture a greater share of the value generated by the global energy transition.

However, turning these ambitions into reality will require more than increased mineral production. It will also depend on the development of local industries, skilled labour and infrastructure capable of supporting large-scale manufacturing.

While foreign capital is driving an expansion of Zambia’s mining sector, trade unions say local workers are yet to see meaningful improvements in their working conditions.

“Inasmuch as the copper prices are going up and we have seen an increase in the amount of investments, we are experiencing same employment conditions – things are not any better for a mineworker,” Stephen Mwaanga, secretary of the National Union of Miners and Allied Workers, told Al Jazeera.

Despite higher copper prices, Mwaanga said, mining companies were also grappling with elevated production costs, including higher fuel prices, which he linked to the US-Israel war on Iran, affecting traffic via the Strait of Hormuz.

The wider Southern African region has also faced drought conditions associated with El Nino, putting additional pressure on electricity supplies. Zambia’s heavy reliance on hydropower makes the mining industry particularly vulnerable to reduced water levels, forcing the country to seek electricity imports and alternative sources of power.

Reliable electricity supplies are critical to sustaining the expansion of an industry that is central to Zambia’s economy.

“We need to strike a balance between improving the workers’ conditions of service and the challenges that these mining companies are facing,” Mwaanga said.

The challenge for the government is therefore not simply to attract more mining capital, but to ensure that increased production translates into better employment conditions and wider economic opportunities for Zambians.

Beyond workers’ welfare, the rapid expansion of mining is raising concerns about its environmental consequences, particularly in communities already affected by pollution.

Eugene Mulenga, a human rights defender, fears the government’s drive to increase mineral production could place enormous pressure on the environment.

In February 2025, a structural failure at a tailings dam operated by Chinese-owned Sino-Metals Leach Zambia in Copperbelt released acidic, metal-laden mining waste into the Chambishi Stream. The pollution spread downstream into the Mwambashi and Kafue river systems, raising serious concerns about water quality, aquatic life and the livelihoods of communities dependent on the waterways.

A subsequent environmental assessment by the Zambia Environmental Management Agency documented the extent of the ecological damage and the effects of the discharge on affected waterways.

The incident exposed the environmental risks associated with mining expansion and renewed questions about the ability of regulatory authorities to monitor operations and enforce environmental standards.

Other pollution incidents have also been reported at mining operations, adding to concerns about the industry’s environmental footprint.

Zambia’s push to increase copper production to 3 million tonnes annually by 2031 has therefore intensified calls for stronger environmental safeguards and greater accountability from mining companies.

For common Zambians and local businesses, the benefits of the country’s growing mining investments also remain a subject of debate.

In an effort to ensure more mining-related spending circulates within the domestic economy, the government introduced local-content regulations, which require mining companies to allocate at least 20 percent of their annual procurement budgets for core mining goods and services to local suppliers in 2026. The threshold is scheduled to rise to 25 percent after one year, with further increases planned.

The policy is intended to strengthen indigenous businesses, create opportunities for Zambian suppliers and ensure a greater share of economic benefits from mining remains within the country.

But as Zambia positions itself to become a key supplier of minerals critical to the global energy transition, the question remains whether the investment boom will deliver meaningful improvements in citizens’ lives, particularly those living and working in mining communities.

For Mulenga, the economic ambitions must not come at the expense of communities whose livelihoods depend on the environment.

“What we have discovered is that most farmers and poor people who depend directly on these water bodies near the mining sites are being affected by the increasing mining activity,” he told Al Jazeera.

articles.title: Eisenkot says Netanyahu can’t remain Israel PM amid alleged vote meddling
articles.excerpt: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cannot “remain at the helm of government for even one more minute” amid reports alleging Netanyahu’s office engaged i...
articles.body_text:
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cannot “remain at the helm of government for even one more minute” amid reports alleging Netanyahu’s office engaged in electoral interference.

Eisenkot, tasked with forming Israel’s new government, launched a scathing attack on his rival on Sunday, just a few hours after representatives of the two men met to discuss the possible formation of a national unity government.

“The conduct of outgoing Prime Minister Netanyahu and his inner circle poses a tangible, direct and immediate threat to Israeli democracy,” Eisenkot wrote on X.

Israeli broadcaster Channel 12 published a report earlier on Sunday alleging Netanyahu’s chief of staff, Ido Norden, lodged a complaint with the police commissioner’s office against members of the United Arab List (Ra’am) party on the eve of Israel’s October 27 election.

Norden reportedly directed police officers to an alleged intelligence source who was a former employee of Netanyahu’s office.

Based on information from the source, about 14 police officers raided the homes of three Ra’am members without a warrant and arrested them on suspicion of bribery to incentivise voting, according to Channel 12.

Netanyahu subsequently launched a campaign against Arab-led parties throughout election day. After they won a record 19 seats, he made unproven accusations of electoral fraud.

The three men were released after police determined the information from the purported intelligence source was unfounded.

The Channel 12 report also alleged that David Zini, the head of Israel’s internal intelligence agency Shin Bet, requested the attorney general’s office to wiretap five Palestinian-Israeli Knesset members on election day over suspected election interference, but the request was later rejected.

“I call for an immediate investigation into the affair and for the police and the Shin Bet to immediately clarify the details that have been published,” said Eisenkot, a former army chief.

Netanyahu’s Likud party called Eisenkot’s statement “outrageous incitement” against the prime minister.

On Friday, Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of fuelling a “racist and violent” campaign against Palestinian citizens of Israel during the elections to cling to power.

Netanyahu renewed his appeal to Eisenkot to form a unity government on Saturday, but the opposition leader called the plea a “bluff”.

However, Eisenkot had confirmed talks between his Yashar party and the Likud party over the proposal for a shared government.

Neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot’s bloc has yet secured the 61 seats needed to form a government.

articles.title: ‘Loaded with potential’: stage version of TV smash It’s a Sin has the dancefloor at its heart
articles.excerpt:
Exclusive: Trailer released for Rambert’s version of Russell T Davies’s show about friendship amid the 80s Aids crisis and the ‘extraordinary freedom’ of clubbing

Russell T Davies’s award-winning ser...
articles.body_text:
Exclusive: Trailer released for Rambert’s version of Russell T Davies’s show about friendship amid the 80s Aids crisis and the ‘extraordinary freedom’ of clubbing

Russell T Davies’s award-winning series It’s a Sin, about young gay friends living through the Aids crisis in 1980s London, is getting a new life as a dance piece, with a trailer released on Monday ahead of an opening at Aviva Studios in Manchester in February.

“We had a few approaches, but a lot of people wanted to make it a musical, which made my heart sink slightly,” said Davies. “I always imagined an aria between those two women on the seafront at the end and I thought: ‘Oh, that could be so terrible!’” Dance was different, he said. “It felt so original and so pure. The story distils down to these emotional moments that are going to be done so beautifully on stage.”

The idea came from Benoit Swan Pouffer, artistic director of Rambert, which celebrated its centenary this year with a commitment to bringing in new audiences, in part by reinventing familiar titles, as in its dance version of Peaky Blinders. “Dance needs to be democratised and this is the way to do it,” said Pouffer, who is choreographing It’s a Sin.

Davies has a cameo in the trailer, although his own dance career peaked with a performance for Princess Diana with West Glamorgan youth theatre (she told him he should continue to “Dance, dance, dance!”). The dancefloor, however, has always been an inspiration. “They’re such potent places, so loaded with potential.” Davies spent many nights in the clubs of Manchester’s Canal Street, watching lives play out to music. “Those dancefloors were places of such extraordinary freedom,” he said. “Especially in the 80s, with that layer of secrecy. That’s where you’d be out – you might not be out at home – becoming the person you aspired to be.”

The dance world was notably affected by the Aids epidemic. “I had friends and colleagues who left us too early,” said Pouffer. He was dancing in the US in the mid-90s, and saw as much stigma about HIV and Aids in the dance world as anywhere else. “There was shame, it was hidden. Even Alvin Ailey, that’s not what we said [that he died of an Aids-related illness] when he passed. Even now there is still a stigma,” said Pouffer. “The trauma, you put it in a little capsule and you don’t talk about it. Now we have this young PrEP generation who don’t know how traumatic it was. The closest they can think of is Covid,” he suggested. “Remember in the beginning when we didn’t know anything about the virus?”

Pouffer also wants to convey the excitement and creative spark of the era. “The fashion, the music, the dance of the 80s, it was one of the peaks of history,” he said. There will be video and narration to help tell the story, with scripts by Kaite O’Reilly. Davies is an executive producer, as are Pet Shop Boys, whose title song will feature alongside an original soundtrack by Roman GianArthur.

When Davies originally pitched the TV series he was turned down by all the major UK networks, even Channel 4, which eventually commissioned it. “It was simply an assumption that it would be miserable, even when they had the first script to read,” he said.

The series went on to be a huge hit. “Not a week goes past without someone stopping me in the street,” said Davies. Yet it was hard to celebrate, “because no matter how proud we were, it’s a story that’s founded on a lot of deaths”.

There is “a great heaviness at the heart of it, a great sadness and loss,” he continued. “But we told it with joy and vigour and life. The most important thing is to remember the life that those people had, not the death … I think the show worked because it turned around and said: ‘Hey, we loved those boys. Remember the love.’”

It’s a Sin is on tour from 16 February to 13 November 2027

articles.title: Mexican drug lord Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo dies age 80
articles.excerpt:
Mexican prison police secured the hospital where Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo was admitted earlier this week

Notorious Mexican drug lord Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo has died in hospital aged 80.

Féli...
articles.body_text:
Mexican prison police secured the hospital where Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo was admitted earlier this week

Notorious Mexican drug lord Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo has died in hospital aged 80.

Félix Gallardo was widely considered one of the biggest drug smugglers in history and is credited with building an alliance between criminal groups in Colombia and his own Mexican cartel.

Known as The Godfather or the 'Boss of Bosses', Félix Gallardo was the head of the all-powerful Guadalajara Cartel, which reigned over Mexican drug trafficking at the height of the cocaine boom of the 1980s.

At the time, it created a new modus operandi in the illegal drug trade which endures to this day. He had been in state custody since 1989.

The name Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo will echo through the annals of drug-trafficking history more than any other except perhaps Pablo Escobar's.

He led the organisation which revolutionised drug smuggling in the region by entering into partnership with the Colombian cartels, particularly Escobar's Medellín Cartel, to combine production in the Andes with Mexican transportation across the border into the United States.

At one point an estimated 80% of all cocaine that entered the US came from the Medellín Cartel. Félix Gallardo and his organisation played a major role in smuggling it in.

At its height, the Guadalajara Cartel under Félix Gallardo influenced Mexican politics and law enforcement, controlling entire police networks and state governorships.

In 1985, the net started to tighten around the leaders of the cartel following the torture and murder of a DEA agent, Enrique 'Kiki' Camarena.

Camarena had angered them after he had discovered and then destroyed a vast marijuana plantation in Chihuahua, which belonged to the criminal group.

His death sparked one of the biggest manhunts the US government has ever launched in North America.

In 1989, Félix Gallardo was captured and sentenced to decades in prison. In ill health, he was placed under house arrest since 2022 and died in hospital in his native Guadalajara.

In the 1980s, Joaquin 'El Chapo' Guzmán was introduced to Félix Gallardo, who put him in charge of handling logistics for his drug organisation.

From the subsequent break-up of Félix Gallardo's organisation after his arrest, the Sinaloa Cartel emerged, led by Guzmán, now another man synonymous with large-scale drug trafficking.

In 2019, Guzmán was sentenced to life in prison for charges including drug trafficking and money laundering following one of the most high-profile trials in recent US history.

articles.title: NTSB details warning whistles and emergency orders before tanker collision capsized New Orleans riverboat
articles.excerpt: NTSB investigators detail a steering problem, warning whistles and emergency anchor orders in the minutes before the Atlantic Asphalt struck the docked American Heritage in New Orleans. (Credit: WVUE)...
articles.body_text:
NTSB investigators detail a steering problem, warning whistles and emergency anchor orders in the minutes before the Atlantic Asphalt struck the docked American Heritage in New Orleans. (Credit: WVUE)

A tanker suffered a steering problem about two minutes before slamming into a docked New Orleans riverboat Friday, federal investigators said Sunday, detailing warning whistles, calls for help and emergency orders before the collision.

The Atlantic Asphalt was heading upriver near the Crescent City Connection Bridge at about 12:26 p.m. when its rudder remained turned to the right, sending the ship toward the Mississippi River’s east bank, National Transportation Safety Board senior marine accident investigator Bart Barnum said.

The tanker struck American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage at about 12:28 p.m. The riverboat capsized in about 22 minutes, according to preliminary information presented by the NTSB.

NEW ORLEANS BOAT CRASH CALLED ‘MIRACLE ON THE MISSISSIPPI’ AS EVERYONE IS ACCOUNTED FOR, OFFICIALS SAY

Investigators downloaded more than nine hours of data from the tanker’s voyage data recorder, including bridge audio, rudder angle, engine RPM, course and speed.

The recordings captured sounds consistent with the ship’s whistle, warnings and requests for assistance over its marine radio, commands to deploy anchors and emergency shiphandling orders, Barnum said.

11-NIGHT CARIBBEAN CRUISE ABRUPTLY CANCELED AFTER COAST GUARD DETAINS SHIP

Officials described the steering problem as a "steering casualty," but cautioned that the term does not establish what went wrong.

"It could be many different things. That is something that we are investigating very closely," Barnum said.

AT LEAST 6 PEOPLE INJURED AFTER BOSTON DUCK BOAT OVERTURNS NEAR ENTRANCE TO POPULAR TOURIST ATTRACTION

Tugboats surround the Atlantic Asphalt tanker in New Orleans following its collision with the docked American Heritage river cruiser on Nov. 13, 2026. (Kat Ramirez for Fox News Digital)

NTSB board member John DeLeeuw said investigators have data on the tanker’s speed but are still analyzing it before releasing it publicly. Video showed anchors were down, but investigators are still determining which ones were deployed and how far, he said.

The findings follow a frantic rescue effort that officials said left everyone aboard the American Heritage alive. Roughly 100 people were pulled from the Mississippi River, while responders evacuated more than 80 before the vessel overturned, Port of New Orleans Harbor Police Chief Melanie Montroll said Saturday.

TWO DEAD, INCLUDING INFANT, AFTER BOAT CAPSIZES IN NEW YORK HARBOR; 12 RESCUED

"This is a miracle. It is a literal miracle on the Mississippi," Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry said Friday.

Eight people remained hospitalized Saturday, including two in serious condition. The other six were stable, officials said.

FBI INVESTIGATES SUSPECTED HOMICIDE ABOARD MSC SEASCAPE CRUISE SHIP AFTER SUDDEN RETURN TO TEXAS

The NTSB said Sunday that 140 passengers and 50 crew members were aboard the riverboat, a total of 190.

New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno also said the American Heritage’s captain was injured but stayed aboard until passengers and crew were accounted for, becoming the last person to leave.

MOM LOSES GRIP ON DAUGHTER AS PASSENGER FERRY CAPSIZES WITH 20 PEOPLE STILL MISSING

"Every moment of the critical time [Friday], he did not want to leave his ship," Moreno said Saturday.

Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham said Saturday that crews were preparing to remove 16,000 gallons of fuel before salvage operations, warning that removing the capsized vessel could take weeks. DeLeeuw said Sunday that divers had been in the water, with salvage work overseen by the Coast Guard and salvage companies.

UNLICENSED NYC BOAT OPERATOR ALLEGEDLY IGNORED SAFETY WARNINGS BEFORE MOTHER, BABY DIED IN CAPSIZING: FEDS

Port of New Orleans collision map. (Google Maps)

Interviews with American Heritage crew members were underway Sunday. Interviews with the Atlantic Asphalt’s crew were scheduled to begin Monday and continue through the week, Barnum said.

The NTSB expects to release a preliminary report within about 30 days. Sunday’s briefing was its last planned on-site news conference, DeLeeuw said, with further updates to be posted online.

Fox News Digital's Brittany Miller contributed to this report.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

NTSB investigators detail a steering problem, warning whistles and emergency anchor orders in the minutes before the Atlantic Asphalt struck the docked American Heritage in New Orleans. (Credit: WVUE)

A tanker suffered a steering problem about two minutes before slamming into a docked New Orleans riverboat Friday, federal investigators said Sunday, detailing warning whistles, calls for help and emergency orders before the collision.

The Atlantic Asphalt was heading upriver near the Crescent City Connection Bridge at about 12:26 p.m. when its rudder remained turned to the right, sending the ship toward the Mississippi River’s east bank, National Transportation Safety Board senior marine accident investigator Bart Barnum said.

The tanker struck American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage at about 12:28 p.m. The riverboat capsized in about 22 minutes, according to preliminary information presented by the NTSB.

NEW ORLEANS BOAT CRASH CALLED ‘MIRACLE ON THE MISSISSIPPI’ AS EVERYONE IS ACCOUNTED FOR, OFFICIALS SAY

Investigators downloaded more than nine hours of data from the tanker’s voyage data recorder, including bridge audio, rudder angle, engine RPM, course and speed.

The recordings captured sounds consistent with the ship’s whistle, warnings and requests for assistance over its marine radio, commands to deploy anchors and emergency shiphandling orders, Barnum said.

11-NIGHT CARIBBEAN CRUISE ABRUPTLY CANCELED AFTER COAST GUARD DETAINS SHIP

Officials described the steering problem as a "steering casualty," but cautioned that the term does not establish what went wrong.

"It could be many different things. That is something that we are investigating very closely," Barnum said.

AT LEAST 6 PEOPLE INJURED AFTER BOSTON DUCK BOAT OVERTURNS NEAR ENTRANCE TO POPULAR TOURIST ATTRACTION

Tugboats surround the Atlantic Asphalt tanker in New Orleans following its collision with the docked American Heritage river cruiser on Nov. 13, 2026. (Kat Ramirez for Fox News Digital)

NTSB board member John DeLeeuw said investigators have data on the tanker’s speed but are still analyzing it before releasing it publicly. Video showed anchors were down, but investigators are still determining which ones were deployed and how far, he said.

The findings follow a frantic rescue effort that officials said left everyone aboard the American Heritage alive. Roughly 100 people were pulled from the Mississippi River, while responders evacuated more than 80 before the vessel overturned, Port of New Orleans Harbor Police Chief Melanie Montroll said Saturday.

TWO DEAD, INCLUDING INFANT, AFTER BOAT CAPSIZES IN NEW YORK HARBOR; 12 RESCUED

"This is a miracle. It is a literal miracle on the Mississippi," Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry said Friday.

Eight people remained hospitalized Saturday, including two in serious condition. The other six were stable, officials said.

FBI INVESTIGATES SUSPECTED HOMICIDE ABOARD MSC SEASCAPE CRUISE SHIP AFTER SUDDEN RETURN TO TEXAS

The NTSB said Sunday that 140 passengers and 50 crew members were aboard the riverboat, a total of 190.

New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno also said the American Heritage’s captain was injured but stayed aboard until passengers and crew were accounted for, becoming the last person to leave.

MOM LOSES GRIP ON DAUGHTER AS PASSENGER FERRY CAPSIZES WITH 20 PEOPLE STILL MISSING

"Every moment of the critical time [Friday], he did not want to leave his ship," Moreno said Saturday.

Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham said Saturday that crews were preparing to remove 16,000 gallons of fuel before salvage operations, warning that removing the capsized vessel could take weeks. DeLeeuw said Sunday that divers had been in the water, with salvage work overseen by the Coast Guard and salvage companies.

UNLICENSED NYC BOAT OPERATOR ALLEGEDLY IGNORED SAFETY WARNINGS BEFORE MOTHER, BABY DIED IN CAPSIZING: FEDS

Port of New Orleans collision map. (Google Maps)

Interviews with American Heritage crew members were underway Sunday. Interviews with the Atlantic Asphalt’s crew were scheduled to begin Monday and continue through the week, Barnum said.

The NTSB expects to release a preliminary report within about 30 days. Sunday’s briefing was its last planned on-site news conference, DeLeeuw said, with further updates to be posted online.

Fox News Digital's Brittany Miller contributed to this report.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

articles.title: US officials recover audio from ‘Mississippi miracle’ cruise ship and tanker crash
articles.excerpt:
Tank vessel suffered sudden steering failure two minutes before slamming into docked riverboat near New Orleans

Federal safety investigators with the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) recov...
articles.body_text:
Tank vessel suffered sudden steering failure two minutes before slamming into docked riverboat near New Orleans

Federal safety investigators with the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) recovered audio and released a preliminary timeline on Sunday of a collision between a cruise ship and a tanker vessel in the Mississippi River on Friday.

The data was retrieved after more than 30 people were injured when a tanker collided with a docked cruise ship – American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage riverboat – near the port of New Orleans on Friday at about 12.30pm. All passengers aboard the cruise ship have been accounted for, officials said.

The tank vessel suffered a sudden steering failure two minutes before slamming into the docked riverboat, causing it to tip on to its side, officials said.

“It experienced the steering casualty, resulting in the rudder remaining to starboard,” said Bart Barnum, senior marine accident investigator for the NTSB’s office of marine safety, during a media briefing on Sunday. “Following the steering casualty, the Atlantic Asphalt veered to starboard toward the east bank of the river.”

Before the collision, audio collected by officials captured “the ship’s whistle, warnings and requests for assistance broadcasted over the vessel’s marine radio, commands to deploy the vessel’s anchors, and emergency ship handling orders”, according to Barnum.

The NTSB is leading the safety investigation alongside the US Coast Guard, as well as American Cruise Lines and representatives from the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the tanker’s flag state.

A preliminary report is expected to be published within 30 days.

Images and videos of the collision have been circulating online. The father of a cruise ship worker who survived the collision spoke about the moment his daughter called him in the middle of the incident.

“She’s FaceTiming me hysterically in a lifejacket in the middle of the Mississippi River crying, ‘Dad, dad, I had to jump off the boat,’” said Wayne Hager in an interview with Good Morning America over the weekend. “I’m hearing people screaming and yelling in the background and kind of like some, I don’t know, like metal grinding noises or whatever.”

Video of Leelah Hager posted on social media later shows her in the water wearing a life vest immediately after the collision between the Atlantic Asphalt tanker and the cruise ship, which had about 190 passengers and crew aboard. Other images of the incident show how the tanker caused the American Heritage to capsize.

New Orleans port officials filed a lawsuit seeking more than $1m in damages from the owner and operator of the asphalt tanker. Four crew members of the American Heritage filed a separate lawsuit against Nave Shipping and Thome Ship Management, which oversee the tanker, claiming they “suffered significant and life changing injuries to their mind and body”, according to the suit.

According to the document, the collision caused the cruise ship to partially sink, throwing the crew members and passengers of the American Heritage “overboard into the Mississippi River, not knowing if they were going to live or die”, the lawsuit reads.

The crew members of American Heritage are alleging negligence, gross negligence, carelessness or fault of the managers of the tanker.

articles.title: DHS chief Mullin says Iran poses daily threat to Trump and his family amid drone concerns
articles.excerpt: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin joins 'The Sunday Briefing' to discuss the agency's efforts to combat hostile drone technology and Iranian threats targeting President Donald Trump and top...
articles.body_text:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin joins 'The Sunday Briefing' to discuss the agency's efforts to combat hostile drone technology and Iranian threats targeting President Donald Trump and top administration officials. Mullin also addresses the massive FAA flight ground stop, pushing back on rumors of a cyberattack.

Department of Homeland Security (DHS) chief Markwayne Mullin warned that President Donald Trump and his family remain top targets of threats from Iran, saying on "The Sunday Briefing" that officials receive intelligence about potential threats daily as concerns grow over the use of drones.

"Well, every single day during our presidential briefings, we receive aspirational threats from Iran. We know that President Trump — and his family — is target number one," Mullin said.

Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said President Donald Trump and his family are Iran's top targets. (REUTERS/Annabelle Gordon)

Mullin's remarks came amid questions about a report alleging Israeli intelligence had identified a potential Iranian plot involving explosive-laden drones targeting Trump. While he did not confirm the specific report, Mullin said officials were aware of threats.

Mullin also called countering unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) his "number one issue," citing increasingly sophisticated drone technology, cartel activity along the southern border and vulnerabilities at major public gatherings.

US MILITARY TOOK DOWN APPROXIMATELY 100 SUSPECTED CARTEL DRONES AT SOUTHERN BORDER IN AUGUST

"Our counter-UAS measures need help, and DHS is leading that, because we encounter more drones on our southern border because of the cartels and the fight we're having with them every single day trying to get drugs into the United States. And we're seeing new technologies that we're having a hard time defeating right now," he continued.

A new law allows law enforcement in Arizona to shoot down drones suspected of participating in criminal activity along the U.S.-Mexico border. (iStock)

Mexican cartels are reported to be using commercial and modified drones to watch U.S. security personnel, map patrol routines and support smuggling corridors along the southern border as authorities expand efforts to disable the aircraft.

US MILITARY BASES ARE ‘ILL-EQUIPPED’ TO STOP DRONE SWARMS, TOP COMMANDER REVEALS AFTER RUBIO'S UAP WARNING

The U.S. military detected 378 drone incursions along the border during the previous 30 days, Brig. Gen. Brian Filler of Joint Task Force-Southern Border told reporters. He said the trend was increasing, and the aircraft were typically commercial drones with cameras used for surveillance tied to smuggling and human trafficking.

Mullin said drone threats extend well beyond the southern border, pointing to security concerns at major sporting events and other large gatherings.

During the FIFA World Cup, for instance, Mullin said law enforcement encountered more than 2,000 drones, confiscated 700 and made multiple arrests. He noted that Los Angeles will host the Olympics in 2028.

But the DHS secretary warned that drone security is also needed at everyday gatherings, including high school football games, parades and professional sporting events.

"There are holes in our counter-UAS ability to be kinetic and bring down real threats," Mullin said, adding that he was coordinating with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on the matter due to issues of airspace clearance.

Mullin said he has established a dedicated counter-drone department within DHS as the agency works to address gaps in its ability to neutralize potential threats.

Fox News Digital's Armando Regil Velasco contributed to this report.

Max Bacall is an associate editor for Fox News Digital covering media, culture and comedy.

articles.title: Trident nuclear submarine concludes record underwater deployment
articles.excerpt:
HMS Vengeance’s seven-month patrol prompts fears over slow pace of maintenance of ageing fleet and strain on crew

A Trident nuclear submarine has concluded a record seven-month deployment, returning ...
articles.body_text:
HMS Vengeance’s seven-month patrol prompts fears over slow pace of maintenance of ageing fleet and strain on crew

A Trident nuclear submarine has concluded a record seven-month deployment, returning to the Faslane naval base in Scotland where its crew was greeted by the defence secretary, Wes Streeting.

HMS Vengeance began its patrol on 12 April and spent 217 days submerged before returning on Sunday, having left the country when Keir Starmer was in Downing Street and Manchester United were third in the Premier League.

Its tour surpasses the previous 205-day record set by HMS Vanguard, and has raised questions about the strains placed on sailors and the reliability of ageing submarines sent on the extended missions.

“Patrols are getting longer and longer,” said David Cullen, a nuclear expert with the Basic thinktank. “The fleet was designed around three-month tours, and that was considered to be a long time to be stuck underwater in a metal box with no contact with the outside world.”

The increase in the time spent at sea reflects the slow pace of submarine maintenance, prompting Labour to blame spending cuts implemented by the Conservatives, though naval chiefs insist there is a plan for improvement.

Streeting said the length of time the crew had spent submerged did not “sit lightly” with him.

Streeting, who was accompanied in Faslane by the first secretary of state, Lou Haigh, added: “It makes me feel even more indebted to the crew for the service they’ve given to the country, for the commitment they show, the dedication, the professionalism, the expertise.

“I think the whole country can be extraordinarily proud of our submariners and of our nuclear deterrent.”

He described the nuclear patrols as the “ultimate national endeavour” and thanked the returning submariners for their “dedicated, heroic service” which he said was the model of patriotism.

HMS Vengeance is one of four submarines that carryBritain’s Trident nuclear missiles. A boat is at sea at all times, so the UK could launch strikes even if land-based systems had been destroyed in a nuclear war.

When the Vanguard class of submarines was brought into service in the 1990s, they were designed to carry three to four months of food for the crew of about 140, and deployments of more than 100 days were considered highly exceptional. Missions now start with tinned food crammed into corridors and other available spaces.

Each submarine has to keep its location secret so it cannot be targeted, meaning it also cannot be resupplied. The boats maintain radio silence and so the crew cannot message out on the long deployments, though they can receive news and other information.

Such is the length of the patrols that the return of a Trident submarine, known as a “day zero”, has become a political event. Starmer made an unannounced visit when the last patrol ended in April, praising the crew on their return.

There have been worries about the psychological impact of the patrols on the crew members, who have to spend seven months underwater in a boat 150 metres long, at a time when the Royal Navy is struggling to recruit new personnel.

Last week, the head of the Royal Navy, Gen Sir Gwyn Jenkins, said he had “nothing but tremendous respect” for the Trident sailors, but added that the UK needed to “improve our submarine maintenance” to allow faster turnaround.

The submarine service, in line with the rest of the navy, has a “no touching rule” – prohibiting physical intimacy on board – though the service has had to contend with allegations of sexual abuse and harassment during deployments.

In October 2024, the then first sea lord was forced to issue an apology to women – who make up about 10% of the navy – who had suffered “misogyny, bullying and other unacceptable behaviours” in the submarine service.

The navy conducted an inquiry after a whistleblower, Sophie Brook, complained of a “constant campaign of sexual bullying” from male sailors. Reports of rape, physical and verbal abuse were examined in a heavily redacted report.

Trident submarines can carry 40 nuclear warheads, with enough destructive power to destroy Moscow and several other major Russian cities, and a letter from the prime minister to tell the captain how to proceed in the event it is determined the UK no longer exists after an all-out nuclear attack.

Such is the length of the boat’s patrol it will still be carrying Starmer’s letter, though the replacement submarine on rotation will have Andy Burnham’s instructions, written in longhand in the days after he took over at Downing Street.

In July, Labour announced a £26bn, 10-year plan to invest in Britain’s three main naval bases, at Faslane, the operational home of the Trident submarines, Devonport and Portsmouth, as part of a wider increase in defence spending.

However, the first of the replacements for the four Vanguard class submarines, HMS Dreadnought, is not expected to be ready until about 2032, meaning that the old boats have at least five more years to remain in service.

“The inherent risks of operating submarines are being pushed by them being run as they are. At the end of the submarines’ design life they should be run gently, not as hard as they are,” Cullen said.

The best public interest journalism relies on first-hand accounts from people in the know. If you have something to share on this subject, you can contact us confidentially using the following methods:

The Guardian app has a tool to send tips about stories. Messages are end to end encrypted and concealed within the routine activity that every Guardian mobile app performs. This prevents an observer from knowing that you are communicating with us at all, let alone what is being said.

If you don’t already have the Guardian app, download it (iOS/Android) and go to the menu. Select ‘Secure Messaging’.

Our guide at theguardian.com/tips lists several ways to contact us securely, and discusses the pros and cons of each.

articles.title: Estonia to close all border crossings with Russia after attack on drone maker
articles.excerpt:
Authorities say Russian intelligence service ordered attack Estonian PM links to Tallinn’s support for Ukraine

Estonia will close all its border crossings with Russia from 1 December after a suspecte...
articles.body_text:
Authorities say Russian intelligence service ordered attack Estonian PM links to Tallinn’s support for Ukraine

Estonia will close all its border crossings with Russia from 1 December after a suspected sabotage attack on a drone maker in the Baltic state over the weekend, which authorities said was ordered by Russia’s GRU military intelligence service.

On Saturday morning, eight people were detained during an attempted attack on Threod Systems, a defence company that manufactures long-range attack and reconnaissance drones. No injuries or damage were reported after the company’s security team responded to the incident.

Estonia’s internal security service, Kapo, said on Sunday the attack was carried out “with the aim of causing an explosion and setting the building on fire”. Authorities have requested a court order for five of those detained to remain in custody, Estonia’s public broadcaster ERR reported.

The Estonian prime minister, Kristen Michal, said the border closure was needed to reduce the risk of further attacks and “send a clear message that attacks on Estonia’s defence industry and defence capabilities” were unacceptable.

He linked the attacks with Estonia’s continuing support for Ukraine. “Russia’s aim is to make us afraid, make us hesitate and weaken our support for Ukraine. Estonia’s response is the opposite. We will strengthen our security, work even more closely with businesses and our allies, increase pressure on Russia and continue supporting Ukraine,” Michal said.

The Estonian foreign minister, Margus Tsahkna, echoed the warning, saying: “Russia must understand that hostile actions against Estonia come with consequences. Attempts to intimidate, destabilise, or undermine our security will not go unanswered.”

Estonia operates three border crossings with Russia – Narva in the north, and Koidula and Luhamaa in the south. The authorities did not specify how long the closure would be.

It is the second attempted attack on an Estonian defence company that authorities have attributed to Russia, after an arson attack at Milrem Robotics in August.

In September, Kapo said it was confident that incident was “a deliberate and pre-planned attack carried out on behalf of Russian special services”. The agency also said it fitted a pattern of Russian attacks targeting defence and drone companies, particularly those with links to Ukraine.

At the time Estonia summoned Russia’s chargé d’affaires over the attack, but the Kremlin denied any link to Russia, saying it was a “baseless” and “ill-considered” accusation “with absolutely no relation to reality”.

Several European intelligence services have repeatedly warned of potential attacks against defence companies and growing Russian attempts to recruit citizens in EU and Nato countries on messaging platforms online to carry out acts of sabotage.

Michal noted that the weekend’s arrests came after security agencies told the defence industry of potential risks. “We do not warn about these threats without reason. Preparedness matters, and this time it clearly paid off,” he said.

The Russian foreign ministry spokesperson, Maria Zakharova, told state news agency Tass: “... If ‌these are ‌their real plans, then ‌they fit into yet another bout of aggressive and unrestrained Russophobia”.

articles.title: Estonia to close border crossings with Russia after attack on drone maker
articles.excerpt:
Estonia will close its border crossings with Russia, after an attack on an Estonian defence company that Tallinn blames on Moscow.

The foreign minister made the announcement on Sunday, after eight pe...
articles.body_text:
Estonia will close its border crossings with Russia, after an attack on an Estonian defence company that Tallinn blames on Moscow.

The foreign minister made the announcement on Sunday, after eight people were detained overnight in connection with an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems.

Estonian authorities said the attacks had been ordered by Russia’s GRU military intelligence.

Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna wrote on X, “Russia must understand that hostile actions against Estonia come with consequences. Attempts to intimidate, destabilise, or undermine our security will not go unanswered.

“Closing the border crossings will reduce Russia’s ability to conduct hostile activities in Estonia and strengthen our efforts to prevent sanctions circumvention.”

He did not specify how long the border closure would last.

A Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman told state news agency TASS that the plans were “yet another bout of aggressive and unrestrained Russophobia.”

Latvia’s Interior Minister Janis Dombrava thanked Estonia’s Internal Security Service on X, saying that several “Latvian citizens and non-citizens” were arrested.

“Since the collapse of the USSR, there have been people among us who are willing to commit serious crimes in Russia’s interests. We will continue our work to ensure that such people cannot endanger the lives of those who love Latvia and want to live in safety,” Dombrava wrote.

Estonia, a European Union and NATO member state and a strong ally of Ukraine, currently has three open border crossings with Russia at Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula.

Marko Mihkelson, chairman of the Estonian Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, told Al Jazeera that the arrests demonstrated that Estonia was “prepared to respond swiftly to such attacks.”

“It is essential that Russia’s state-sponsored campaign of terror does not remain merely a matter of diplomatic protests, either in Estonia or among our allies elsewhere,” Mihkelson said.

“Russia is waging a shadow war to divide Europe and undermine support for Ukraine. European countries must respond with asymmetric measures of their own. Closing borders with Russia is one such measure.”

articles.title: Iran launches drone attacks against US military base in Bahrain
articles.excerpt:
Strikes cast further doubt on peace talks between Tehran and Washington with increasing risk of escalation

Iran has launched drone attacks against a US military base in Bahrain, casting further doubt...
articles.body_text:
Strikes cast further doubt on peace talks between Tehran and Washington with increasing risk of escalation

Iran has launched drone attacks against a US military base in Bahrain, casting further doubt on peace talks between Tehran and Washington and raising the spectre of escalation.

Blasts sounded over the Gulf nation on Sunday in the second Iranian drone attack in three days in retaliation for US strikes in Iran.

Meanwhile, in Yemen, Iran’s Houthi allies advanced against pro-government forces in the south, opening a potential route to Aden. Iran also claimed that a mine sank an oil supertanker in the strait of Hormuz.

The developments deepened gloom about the chances of any diplomatic breakthrough in the region.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps said they launched six drones targeting a US air defence radar at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base in retaliation for “hostile US actions”. Authorities in Bahrain said air defences intercepted the drones before they reached their targets.

At a press conference in Tehran the foreign ministry spokesperson, Esmaeil Baghaei, said Iran would continue to respond to any military aggression by the US or other states. Asked if the latest strikes indicated a change in Iranian direction as negotiations with the US have stalled, he said Iran was “not waiting for anyone” and was focused on its security.

US forces have conducted a series of strikes against Iranian targets in recent weeks, including Qeshm Island in the strait of Hormuz.

Donald Trump last week called them minor strikes and said Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states had cautioned him against large-scale combat operations.

However, the president also said Washington was no longer seeking a deal with Iran and that he had instructed the vice-president, JD Vance, to switch his focus to alleged corruption and fraud in Democrat-run cities and states.

Vance – who blamed the Republicans’ loss of Congress in midterm elections on the Iran war – had requested a personal meeting with Iranian negotiators to discuss peace terms.

A conflict that began with joint US and Israeli attacks against Iran in February remains at an impasse, with the US maintaining a naval blockade and Iran its chokehold over the strait of Hormuz.

In a separate development, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards claimed that two ships hit mines in the strait of Hormuz and that one, an oil supertanker with 2m barrels of oil, sank. The ships suffered “massive explosions and fire”, said the statement.

There was no immediate independent verification. The US military recently claimed it had cleared all mines from main routes through the waterway.

The strikes against Bahrain suggested Iran has decided on a tit-for-tat response to US attacks.

Bahrain hosts significant US bases, including a forward base that was home to the US Fifth Fleet and US Naval Forces Central Command, operating as a central support hub for military operations in the Middle East.

Tehran repeatedly targeted the kingdom until September, when there was a lull in attacks. That ended on Friday when Iran launched drones against a US radar facility. US Central Command said it shot down two drones without any injury or damage.

The attacks on Sunday prompted sirens and alerts from Bahrain’s authorities urging residents to seek shelter.

“It’s exactly what I was hoping wouldn’t happen: Iranian attacks starting again, with all the worry and uncertainty that go with them,” resident Hayat Ibrahim, 65, told Agence France Presse.

Bahrain’s foreign ministry called the resumption of attacks “heinous aggression” and a flagrant violation of international law.

The kingdom rejected Tehran’s “flimsy pretexts and baseless claims” to target its territory, it said in a statement. “The kingdom also rejects the transformation of its territory into an arena for settling scores and holds Iran fully responsible for these attacks and their consequences.”

Jordan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar condemned the attacks and expressed solidarity with Bahrain.

In Yemen, Saudi Arabia’s campaign against the Iranian-aligned Houthi rebels reeled when forces fighting on behalf of the Yemeni government retreated from the Bab el-Mandeb strait to defend ⁠Aden on the southern ​coast.

“The Southern Armed Forces announce the implementation of ‌a redeployment operation for its forces from Dhubab Airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area, west of Taiz Governorate,” the main military force fighting for Yemen’s government in the south said in a statement.

The admission signalled the apparent failure of a six-week government counteroffensive to drive the Houthis from the mouth of the Red Sea to secure a key oil route.

A Houthi missile strike near Aden killed people and wounded 12 near Aden, AFP reported, citing military and government sources.

articles.title: Clothing factories shut in Bangladesh as workers strike over pay
articles.excerpt:
Protesters in Dhaka, Bangladesh, on Friday demanding a new minimum wage

Dozens of factories in Bangladesh's main clothes-producing area have been shut by workers striking over a higher minimum wage.
...
articles.body_text:
Protesters in Dhaka, Bangladesh, on Friday demanding a new minimum wage

Dozens of factories in Bangladesh's main clothes-producing area have been shut by workers striking over a higher minimum wage.

Nearly 150 sites across the country have been closed in the textile hubs of Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur this weekend.

The garment industry is big business for Bangladesh, generating nearly $40bn (£30bn) in exports every year and making up 10% of the country's total GDP.

Workers are striking over demands for a minimum wage of 30,000 taka (£182) a month.  The minimum monthly wage in Bangladesh is currently 12,500 taka but employees say this is not enough to deal with the cost of living crisis.

On Sunday morning workers massed on the Dhaka-Tangail highway in Gazipur to block the road. Traffic was stopped by the protests for about an hour before police stepped in.

A "No Work No Pay" provision of labour laws allows owners to suspend operations and withhold wages when production is disrupted.

Police Supt Mohammad Amjad Hossain told the BBC officers shut factories in the city after the workers walked out.

He said 13 factories were closed on Saturday night and "sixteen factories were closed during the morning unrest".

Wage protests force hundreds of Bangladesh garment factories to close

The garment industry in Bangladesh employs about four million workers making clothes for big brands including H&M, Primark and Zara.

Bangladesh is the world's second largest exporter of ready- to-wear clothes after China and it is feared that the current unrest could have a knock-on effect for international buyers if it carries on for substantial amount of time.

The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) is calling for protection for factories.

"BGMEA and BKMEA have questioned the justification of continuing to participate in wage board negotiations without any assurance that the factories will be protected," BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan said.

"Garment factories that have been unable to continue production due to the ongoing unrest will remain indefinitely closed from tomorrow under... Bangladesh's labour law."

On 1 November the government formed a minimum wage board to recommend a revised pay structure for workers.

The board, chaired by a senior district judge, said at its first meeting it would finalise any recommendations by the end of November.

Once it is put in place, the revised pay structure is expected to take effect from 1 December.

articles.title: Charlamagne blasts AOC for ‘beating around the bush,’ presses progressives on backing Hakeem Jeffries
articles.excerpt: Radio host Charlamagne tha God criticized Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez’s explanation of leadership elections, pressing her to state whether House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries should face a chall...
articles.body_text:
Radio host Charlamagne tha God criticized Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez’s explanation of leadership elections, pressing her to state whether House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries should face a challenger for speaker.

Radio host Charlamagne tha God blasted Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., for "beating around the bush" about House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries' bid for speaker on Friday — criticizing her explanation of leadership elections instead of directly calling for a challenger.

"I'm watching a lot of beating around the bush. When I see AOC do her tutorial on Instagram Live and I see her getting asked questions … What she really wants to say is, ‘I don’t think Hakeem Jeffrey should be the speaker,'" Charlamagne said during Friday’s episode of the Loud Speakers Network's "The Brilliant Idiots" podcast.

"But, instead of just coming out and saying that and saying, 'Hey, I don't think he should be the speaker of the House. Somebody should challenge him,' she's kind of like beating around the bush telling people why, you know, what the process would look like," he continued. "We don't need a civics lesson."

Charlamagne tha God called out Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for dodging a direct challenge to Hakeem Jeffries' speaker of the house bid. (Derek White/Getty Images for iHeartMedia and The Black Effect Podcast Network)

REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: A USER’S MANUAL TO UPCOMING LEADERSHIP ELECTIONS IN THE HOUSE AND SENATE

The debate over Jeffries' bid has extended beyond podcast commentary to incoming lawmakers weighing their votes.

Rep.-elect Adam Hamawy, D-N.J., said his support should not be taken for granted.

"We're not withholding votes," Hamawy said. "What we’re doing is saying we're undecided. We’re not going to rubber-stamp anything."

Other Democrats have expressed firm support for Jeffries. Rep. Wesley Bell, D-Mo., a Congressional Black Caucus member, left no uncertainty about his choice.

"Hakeem Jeffries all the way," Bell said, in a statement to Fox News Digital.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has emerged as a leading figure on the left and a potential contender in the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential conversation. (Drew Angerer/Getty Images)

WHOOPI GOLDBERG LECTURES DEMOCRATS OVER INFIGHTING ABOUT LEADERSHIP, WARNS 'GET YOUR STUFF TOGETHER'

Charlamagne's assessment followed a social media clip, in which Ocasio-Cortez explained how lawmakers enter leadership races. She encouraged viewers to ask whom their representatives supported rather than simply whether they opposed a particular candidate.

"The question needs to be, ‘Who do you actually want for the speakership? Who is running?’ And right now, both of these races are uncontested," Ocasio-Cortez said.

Charlamagne challenged whether that procedural explanation addressed progressives' disagreements with Jeffries, particularly over military assistance to Israel, and questioned how lawmakers who have described Israel’s actions in Gaza as genocide could support leaders they believe would continue those policies.

"We need, ‘Hey, AOC, simple and plain. As a person, who has said Israel is committing a genocide in Gaza, how can you support leaders that you know who continue to support, in your words, the genocide?’" Charlamagne said.

The radio host said Ocasio-Cortez should directly say she opposes Jeffries instead of explaining leadership procedures. (Paras Griffin/Getty Images)

VAN HOLLEN CHALLENGES SCHUMER FOR SENATE LEADERSHIP AFTER DEMOCRATIC ELECTION SWEEP

Ocasio-Cortez was among the lawmakers listed on a November 2025 resolution, seeking recognition of genocide in Gaza.

Jeffries, who announced his speaker candidacy after the midterms, addressed divisions over Israel assistance during an interview on Wednesday, saying that lawmakers would work together to reconsider how assistance is provided.

"Clearly, dramatic change is necessary," Jeffries said. "I've repeatedly made that point clear, including in July in a letter to the Caucus."

Fox News Digital reached out to the offices of AOC, Jeffries and Schumer for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

CMLL star Thunder Rosa talks to OutKick about the company's streaming partnership with MyAEW.

Blood, guts, staples and a Nintendo Power Glove. It’s a Texas Death match. Did you expect anything else?

Something had to give with the All Elite Wrestling World Trios Championship on the line. Adam Page, Bandido and Brody King were set to defend their titles with all their might against Swerve Strickland, Kofi and Austin Creed. Kofi and Creed came into the match with a little anxiety – having no real interest in getting bloodied up when the match was first announced.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Swerve Strickland, Kofi and Austin Creed capture the World Trios Championship at All Elite Wrestling's Full Gear on Nov. 14, 2026. (Photography by Ricky Havlik)

But Kofi and Creed – who probably weren’t used to the brutality of what a match could bring – gave it their all to help Strickland grab the championship. For the second time in the group’s history, they have the AEW World Trios Championship around their waists.

There were incredible moments in the match and some that made you shield your eyes.

Creed is a noted video game nerd. Who isn’t? But Creed went all the way back to 1989 to pull out something that did damage to King – the Nintendo Power Glove.

The device was kept in a bag that Stokely Hathaway was holding. He called for the duffle bag and pulled out the piece of gaming equipment. It was a thrill to see Creed use his creativity and take it to a, dare I say, new level.

After King bullied him while trying to get the Power Glove wrapped around his wrist, Creed punched the brute in the face and it exploded. No Nintendo Entertainment System necessary.

It looked like it hurt a bit but it was probably the most creative spot of the match. Creed also used a barbed-wire-laden trombone to do some damage to his counterparts earlier in the match.

Adam Page hits Swerve Strickland with a Deadeye at All Elite Wrestling's Full Gear on Nov. 14, 2026. (Photography by Ricky Havlik)

Kofi dropping the boom on Adam Page – more like Adam Pane, am I right? I have some jokes in my back pocket sometimes.

Anyways, Kofi and Creed put two windowpanes on Page as the wrestler was sprawled out on about a half-dozen chairs. Kofi went to the barricade and hit the Boom Drop on Page, breaking the glass all over Page’s torso.

It was interesting to see Kofi get hardcore. He opened the door to something deeper inside of him and it showed. The glass shattered across the ground outside the ring, while Strickland, Kofi and Creed took control of the match.

The way fighters and wrestlers are described in the ring is going "toe-to-toe" or "nose-to-nose." It’s never really staplegun-to-staplegun unless Page and Strickland are involved in a match.

Strickland asked Page to sit down with him – not for a conversation, but for some brutality. Page obliged and the two, with stapleguns in their hands, they used them on each other’s bodies. When their teammates got into the ring, they each received staples for their troubles.

It would not be the last time the two rivals would go for it all in the match. Something much worse came later.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

It was a callback to their Texas Death match at Full Gear in 2023, as Fightful pointed out during the night. Page busted Strickland open and with blood pouring out of his face, Page opened his mouth to get a taste.

This time, it was Strickland who made the gnarliest of decisions to get a taste of Page’s blood. The spot may have divided social media but the storyline and the opportunity was there – Strickland took full advantage.

Page did have the upper hand for a brief moment after the gross moment. But as Page went to slug Strickland with a chair shot, he was stopped dead in his tracks. Strickland was smiling. Page was about to hit him with a chair and he was smiling. Strickland spit the blood he had in his mouth at Page to counter what Page was going to do to him.

Page thought he had the match in the bag. He was setting up Strickland for a string of Buckshot Lariats. He only hit two of them. On the third, Strickland countered. He gave Page a House Call, knocking out his opponent.

Adam Page, Brody King and Bandido (L-R) put skewers into the heads of their opponents at All Elite Wrestling's Full Gear on Nov. 14, 2026. (Photography by Ricky Havlik)

Strickland, Kofi and Creed recaptured the Trios Championship and Strickland made it known that he was the baddest man on the planet.

A fishing trip off the coast of Mexico turned into a pretty memorable outing for OutKast rapper Big Boi, who hauled in a massive 200-pound striped marlin after a 50-minute battle.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

The Grammy-winning rapper, whose real name is Antwan André Patton, shared footage on Saturday from the deep-sea fishing excursion near Cabo San Lucas. In the video, the enormous fish launches itself out of the water as the crew works to bring it alongside the boat.

Outkast's Big Boi snagged a massive striped marlin during a recent trip to Mexico. The rapper frequently shares fishing content on his social media channels. (Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)

And judging by the footage, this fish wasn't going down without a fight.

"Catch of the day 'Striped Marlin' 8 feet 200LBS … took me 50 minutes to get him in the boat #DeepSeaFishing," the rapper wrote.

Not exactly your average afternoon on the water.

A second video shows the 51-year-old Atlanta native posing beside his catch at the marina, where the enormous billfish was hanging by its tail.

NEW HAMPSHIRE FISHERMEN SMASH STATE RECORD BY SNAGGING INSANE 1,116-POUND BLUEFIN TUNA

And this one's getting a permanent place in Big Boi's collection.

The rapper said he plans to have the marlin mounted and shipped back to Atlanta. He also indicated that the fish's meat would be donated to help feed several families, meaning the catch will provide more than just impressive wall decor.

Fishing reels sit on a charter fishing boat heading for a reef in the Sea of Cortez near Puerto Penasco. (2019)

The reported weight is an estimate, as Big Boi mentioned an issue with the scale at the dock.

Striped marlin are among the most sought-after game fish in the waters around Cabo San Lucas. Known for their speed and spectacular aerial displays, they're capable of giving even experienced anglers a serious workout.

Striped marlin carries a sardine in its mouth during the sardine run season in Bahia Magdalena, Baja California Sur, Mexico. (Getty Images)

Big Boi is no stranger to fishing, either. He has previously shared catches of grouper, snapper and triggerfish on social media.

Still, a 200-pound marlin is quite an upgrade.
